link.note: Baptism and marriage confirmed in the Lavenham register (Hammond 1902); father of Sarah Smith by his will (Middlesex Probate 7167). Newly identified in Round 1; probable as John's ancestor (depends on Sarah = Bull Smith's wife, which most authorities accept, and on Temperance's parentage).

summary: John's 11th-great-grandfather; Lavenham clothier's son who became one of Watertown, Massachusetts's largest landowners.
bio: Lavenham register: '1575, Oct. 30, William, son of Thomas Hamond'. Married Elizabeth Paine at Lavenham 9 Jun 1605; children William (1607), Anne (1609), John (1611), Anna (1616), Thomas (1618) and John (1626) baptized there (plus probably 'Marie' 1623 = Sarah). His father died when William was 14 and his mother remarried within five months. He had stood surety for his son William's debts in England. Sailed in the 1630s; his wife followed on the Francis in April 1634 with three children. At Scituate before 1636; freeman of Watertown 1636; one of Watertown's largest landowners (331 acres; estate £457). In 1661 the houses of 'old Warren and Goodman Hammond' were ordered searched for Quakers (the John Warren who emigrated with them, a Hall Street, Melford neighbour). Rev. George Phillips called him 'my brother Hammond'. Will dated July 1662, proved 16 Dec 1672 (Middlesex Probate 7167): 'To Adam Smith, son of daughter, Sarah, if he behave obediently to my wife after my decease, one mare colt and £20 … To daughter, Sarah Smith, £5'; it penalized grandson Thomas if he contested. Hammond-line cousins: Col. John F. Farnsworth (6C6R), S. D. Warren (6C6R), Samuel D. Warren II, Edward Perry Warren, Henry Clarke Warren, Fiske and Cornelia Warren (7C5R).
funFacts: Left his grandson Adam Smith a colt 'if he behave obediently'.
His house was searched for Quakers in 1661.
